evidence: STRUCTURE (no inversion found by design). scoring.toml/score.py/test.sh are byte-identical to the frozen template (diff clean). score.py:40-48: gates (render=0.0, constraints=0.0, all_pass) only zero the reward; scored dims are a weighted mean functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2; functional floor 0.05. Every scored criterion is binary-weighted (functional 44 criteria, total weight 61.0, per-criterion 1/1.5/2 by importance; polish 5 criteria, 9.5; visual 5 equal likert). The weighted sum is monotone in each criterion, the floor is monotone in functional, and function carries 0.6 vs 0.2 craft, so the skill's example inversion ('craft carrying more mass than function') does not occur. GATES: render gate (wrong password refused, then Rafael signs in to a usable workspace) and constraints gate (Rafael adds a Data Analyst candidate via UI, reload still signed in and card present, Observer in an independent context sees exactly one card in Applied) are both public basics (brief lines 7, 17-19; rules s2 'new card starts at the bottom of Applied', s6 drafts survive reload separately from session end). I found no gate that a more complete app is more likely to fail; Data Analyst is a seeded job. DEAD-APP/NEGATIVE CREDIT: functional/prompt.md:13 'Every refusal row needs its own positive control'; refusal rows name controls (hro_activity_refusals 'successful actions' lines are the control', hro_mgr_other_job, hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff 'cannot sign in ... makes this row 0', hro_candidate_private 'receives none of its own data is 0', hro_refusal_status 'If none of these replays was refused, this row is 0'); polish live rows are 0 if no update arrives; hro_pol_earlier_place needs earlier messages to appear above. So a dead or permissive app does not farm refusal/preservation credit. Role replays send the current version first (functional/prompt.md:17), so a stricter app that checks versions is not penalised with 409-masking on role rows. Optimistic vs pessimistic move UI both pass hro_refused_put_back ('A UI that refuses before the card moves ... also passes'). 'Do not deduct the same observed defect in more than one row' (functional:31, polish:24). TRY-A-BROKEN-APP: (a) a near-dead but polished app that clears the floor (>3.05/61, e.g. job_open+add_candidate+reorder) with visual Likert 5 scores about 0.6*0.074+0.2 = 0.244, above a functionally solid but plain app at functional 0.35, polish 0, visual all 1 (0.21). This trade-off comes from the template-controlled 0.6/0.2/0.2 split and 0.05 floor that the skill's delivery profile mandates; it is not strict dominance and not a task-authored defect. (b) Permissive app P (Observer replays accepted) and correct-but-wrong-status app Q (Observer refusals carry 401) each lose one weight-1 row (hro_observer_readonly vs hro_refusal_status): a tie, not an inversion; weight honesty belongs to row 44. TRY-A-CONFORMING-APP: an app that hides or disables the Interview move when Interview is full (prompt line 31 says offering is the app's choice) shows no refusal reason and may lose hro_refused_put_back (weight 2), but the brief also asks 'tell me why', so I record this as row 27/34 wording ambiguity, not a ranking inversion. An app sending messages over a WebSocket may not be cut off by context.setOffline in hro_pol_failed_send (tool-feasibility, row 32/36 territory). UNMEASURED: raw-evidence-index.json scope says 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'; the only runtime evidence is a scripted golden driver (26 PASS groups; hashes verified), which is not a ranking measurement. A credible inversion path stays unmeasured: the functional judge (timeout 9000 s, 14 sequential protocols, many independent contexts and timed observations) scores budget-exhausted outcomes as binary 0 'NOT EXERCISED'. A more complete app makes more successful steps (B, T, U, K, R and V proceed further), so it is likelier to exhaust the budget before A (activity, 2 rows) and D (hro_restart, 1.5) than a weaker app whose earlier protocols end quickly. No mutated-weak-app ranking runs or full configured judge duration exist to rule this out. Colderwater lessons checked: lesson 2 (single documented 1.0/1.5/2.0 weight scheme, consistent here), lesson 4 (gates kept to load/reload/server-backed, satisfied), lesson 16 (no double deduction: functional and polish live rows grade different observables, delivery vs preservation; polish rows score 0 when no update arrives, which correlates with the functional live rows but is monotone), lesson 9 (report-every-step present in both scored prompts).
counterexample: Not a demonstrated inversion. Unmeasured candidate: a complete app exhausts the 9000 s functional judge budget during U/K/R/V and gets NOT EXERCISED = 0 for hro_activity, hro_activity_refusals and hro_restart, while a weaker app that fails B/T early reaches A and D and earns them. The design-level trade-off where a near-dead polished app outscores a plain functional app comes from the template's 0.6/0.2/0.2 split and is not strict dominance.
suggested_fix: No task edit is required for the row as designed. Before clearance, record hash-bound reward-ordering evidence: score the golden plus graded mutants (for example no undo, no live updates, permissive roles, dead UI) with the full configured judge, confirm the ordering is golden > partial > dead, and measure functional judge wall time against the 9000 s budget so truncation does not penalise complete apps.
